第 58 章 Not Everyone Wants to Be a People Manager不是每个人都想做人员经理

Jesse Anderson / 杰西·安德森

— 第 169 页 —

Occasionally, technical people get pushed into management. This can be good—sometimes technical people need coaxing into getting out of their comfort zone and into something new. This also can be bad—such as when a technical person really doesn't want to be a people manager. These forced promotions often come when companies lack a promotion path for their technical tracks. For example, their lead software engineer is incredible, but there is nowhere to promote that person. The company lacks a technical individual contributor title—and pay grade—above some kind of arbitrary limit.

偶尔，技术人员被推上管理岗。这可能是好事——有时候技术人员需要被哄着走出舒适区进入新事物。这也可能是坏事——比如当技术人员真的不想做人员经理时。这些强制晋升通常发生在公司缺乏技术轨道晋升路径时。例如，他们的首席软件工程师非常出色，但没有地方晋升这个人。公司在某种任意上限之上缺乏技术独立贡献者头衔——和薪酬等级。

Looking around they find the need to promote that person into management and that's when the problems begin. I've seen this firsthand a few times and spoken to the individuals who find themselves in a management position that they never wanted or should be in. This is when the individual begins to feel stuck. I've known people whose promotion to manager was publicly announced before they were even asked whether they wanted to be manager. I've had people realize early on that management wasn't for them, but the title and social praise kept them in the position.

环顾四周他们发现需要把那个人晋升到管理层，问题就开始了。我亲眼见过几次，和那些发现自己处在从未想要或不应该在的管理岗位的人谈过。这就是个人开始感觉卡住的时候。我认识一些人，他们晋升经理在被问是否想当经理之前就公开宣布了。我有人早早就意识到管理不适合他们，但头衔和社会赞誉让他们留在那个位置。

It's sad because these people feel there's no other way out of the problem. They're faced with choosing the lesser of three evils: toughing it out, transferring within the company, or quitting the company. More often than not, the person feels the need to quit to save face and move back into an individual contributor position. The quitting part is really a blow to the organization. The person was promoted because they were a great individual contributor and now the organization lost them.

这很悲伤因为这些人觉得没有别的办法走出问题。他们面临在三个祸害中选较轻的一个：硬撑、公司内转岗、或辞职。通常，这个人觉得需要保全面子辞职，回到独立贡献者岗位。辞职这部分对组织真是打击。这个人被晋升是因为他们是优秀的独立贡献者，现在组织失去了他们。

— 第 170 页 —

Whether you're on the receiving end of an unwanted promotion or you're looking for a technical person to promote, the same solution exists: you need to communicate (this will come in handy while you're managing!). This is a time when you should ask questions like these:

无论你是不想要的晋升的接受方，还是你在找一个技术人员晋升，同一个解决方案存在：你需要沟通（这在你管理时会派上用场！）。这是你应该问这些问题的时候：

  • Is going into management one of your goals?进入管理是你的目标之一吗？
  • Is the reason you're needing or wanting to go into management because there isn't a technical individual contributor path that goes high enough?你需要或想进入管理的原因是不是因为没有足够高的技术独立贡献者路径？
  • Given the choice between staying an individual contributor or a manager, which would you choose?在做独立贡献者和经理之间选择，你会选哪个？
  • Are you afraid or leery of going into management because it's something new?你是不是因为管理是新事物而害怕或警惕？

When dealing with this fear, sometimes people will try to manage and code. I tried this and it just doesn't work. I did both jobs poorly. Sitting in meetings all day or trying to code in between meetings just leaves you set up for failure. It's really a Gordian Knot that you need to cut. I wasn't ready to hang up my keyboard and I thought I could do both. I couldn't. I should have done one or the other. I eventually did cut that knot and did much better as a direct result.

应对这种恐惧时，有时候人们会试图既管理又写代码。我试过，就是不行。我两件事都做得很差。整天坐在会议里或试图在会议间隙写代码就是让你失败。这真是一个需要斩断的戈尔迪之结。我没准备好挂起键盘，以为我能两者都做。我不能。我应该只做一件事。我最终斩断了那个结，直接结果是我做得好多了。

If I could do it again, I would ease into the position more. I would understand what it meant to be a good manager rather than what I thought was a good manager (there's even a book about that now). I would spend time looking outside my limited network to find those who truly exemplified and practiced good management skills. I think I based too much of my management style on the (comparatively poor) management styles that had been modeled to me by my previous managers. I would remember that management isn't just about running meetings and scrums. Finally, I would focus on continuous improvement instead of just continuous learning.

如果能重来，我会更渐进地进入这个岗位。我会理解当好经理意味着什么，而不是我以为的好经理（现在甚至有一本关于那的书）。我会花时间在我有限的网络之外找那些真正示范和实践好管理技能的人。我觉得我的管理风格太多基于前经理示范给我的（相对差的）管理风格。我会记住管理不只是开会议和 scrum。最后，我会聚焦持续改进而不只是持续学习。
